title: The Debris Defense: Russia Says It Shot Everything Down. The Footage Says Otherwise.
narrative: Overnight, Russia reported one of the largest drone attacks on Moscow since the war began. Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said roughly 600-620 UAVs flew toward the capital region and claimed 180-201 were destroyed over the area; the Defense Ministry claimed 822 destroyed across Russia. The official framing for every consequence: 'falling debris.' A Wildberries warehouse 25 km from the Kremlin burned. An 83-year-old man was killed in his home. At least six people died across Russia. The manufacturer of the drones that hit the warehouse published the strike footage itself.
telemetry: Moscow Mayor Sobyanin: ~600-620 UAVs flew toward the capital region; claimed 180-201 destroyed over the area (AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, NV)
Russian MoD claimed 822 drones destroyed across Russia overnight (AP)
Wildberries warehouse in Koledino, 25 km from Moscow's center: hit and set ablaze, 3 injured, huge plume of smoke captured on video (Sobyanin via BBC)
Ukrainian defense firm Fire Point published FP-1 strike footage confirming direct hits on the Wildberries logistics hub in Koledino — a complex spanning 200,000+ sq m (NV)
An 83-year-old man was killed when a drone hit a private home in Moscow Oblast — by Gov. Vorobyov's own account a direct strike, not debris (AP/BBC)
At least 6 people killed in Russia overall: 5 in the Rostov region, 1 in Moscow Oblast (AP)
Official counts internally inconsistent: Sobyanin reported 600 drones / 201 destroyed (AP) but also 620 drones / 180 destroyed (NV, Mathrubhumi); none independently verified
Analyst Pavel Felgenhauer: Ukraine bypassed the Moscow region's 'best and most dense antiair defences in the entirety of Russia'; strikes reached the capital's outskirts (Al Jazeera)
Same weekend, a NATO jet downed a drone over Romania (Al Jazeera)

Standing context: Moscow publishes only interception counts, never successful strikes; May set a record with 9,418 claimed drone shootdowns; 'falling debris' is the routine explanation for any damage (ABC News data analysis)
analysis:
Russia's air-defense cover story has one structural weakness: it only reports what it intercepted, and it attributes every consequence to 'falling debris.' This attack broke that mold in three verifiable ways — manufacturer footage, a governor's own admission, and internally contradictory official counts.

First, the footage. Fire Point, the Ukrainian defense firm that makes the FP-1 drone, published strike video of direct hits on the Wildberries logistics hub in Koledino. This is not a claim about what happened. It is a recording of what happened, released by the party that did it. The warehouse complex spans more than 200,000 square meters and sits 25 km from the Kremlin. The plume of smoke over it was captured on independent video and confirmed by Moscow's own mayor, who reported three injured. An explosion at a 200,000 sq m logistics hub 25 km from the center of Moscow is not 'debris.' It is a successful strike.

Second, the governor's account. Moscow Oblast Governor Andrei Vorobyov confirmed that an 83-year-old man was killed when a drone hit his private home. By the governor's own framing — a man killed in his house when the drone itself struck it — this is a direct hit, not an intercepted drone falling. Even Russian officials, in the moments when they are reporting casualties rather than spinning them, cannot maintain the debris fiction.

Third, the numbers. Sobyanin told one outlet 600 drones and 201 destroyed; another outlet got 620 and 180 from him. The Defense Ministry separately claimed 822 destroyed across Russia — a figure that would require the majority of the entire reported wave to have been killed outside the capital region. None of these numbers are independently verifiable, and they do not even agree with each other. When a government's own press releases contradict one another on the same night, the numbers are not data — they are improvisation.

The debris framing is designed to be unfalsifiable in the aggregate: if you only ever report interceptions, and you label all damage as debris, then the air-defense system always works and the enemy never lands a blow. What this attack shows is that the framing only survives when there is no independent evidence. The Fire Point video is independent evidence. The burning warehouse is independent evidence. The dead man in his home is independent evidence. The debris defense requires all three to be invisible, and none of them are.

May's record of 9,418 claimed shootdowns in a single month should be read in this context: when every claim is interception and every impact is debris, the 'success rate' is a narrative choice, not a measurement. The strikes that do land — and the footage that proves they land — are the only data points that escape the filter.

Russia's state media gave the attack only brief mention, per AP — the standard treatment for events the official line cannot fully explain away. But the physical record is already public: the video, the smoke plume, the casualty list, and the contradictory counts. The cover story is collapsing in real time, and this time the receipts were published by the attackers themselves.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Russia says it shot everything down and the damage was 'falling debris.' The record says otherwise: Fire Point published FP-1 strike footage hitting a 200,000 sq m Wildberries hub 25 km from the Kremlin, a governor confirmed a direct drone strike killed an 83-year-old in his home, and Moscow's own counts contradict each other (600 vs 620 drones, 180 vs 201 intercepted). The debris defense only works when there is no footage. There is footage.
